title: Training–Serving Skew
interviewAnswer: Training-serving skew occurs when feature or preprocessing semantics differ between offline training and live inference because of code, time, freshness or source differences.
why: Skew can destroy live quality while offline evaluation still looks good.
intuition: If training computes a feature in SQL and serving computes it differently in application code, model semantics diverge.
deepDive: Prevent skew with shared definitions, point-in-time datasets, schema contracts and parity checks between offline and online values.
commonMistakes: Calling any distribution shift training-serving skew.
Retraining without fixing the feature contract.
production: Continuously sample parity checks and treat feature definitions as versioned APIs.
workedExample: A recommender trained with end-of-day popularity accidentally sees future clicks unavailable at request time.
